A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same work, with methods, equations, experiments, and displays readily matched. All ten pages of each were inspected. Neither contains an appendix or the separately referenced Supplementary Material, so supplementary proofs are outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulations, feature-recovery measurements, and classification accuracy and timing experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1k.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulation and classification results and adds CIFAR-100 accuracy and timing experiments.

M1.justification: The PPCA, LFA, ELF, and HeteroPCA procedures, Algorithms 1–2, SNR criterion, and Mahalanobis/r-score classification remain unchanged. ELF was already present in v1; CIFAR-100 extends evaluation of the existing methods.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 adds CIFAR-100 alongside the retained simulations, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-1k. This is a limited coverage extension within the existing image-classification task using CLIP features.

E2.justification: FSA and soft-thresholding TISP remain the comparison baselines, alongside the same four latent-factor methods. CIFAR-100 uses this existing comparator set. The expanded discussion of earlier SNR methods does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve their sample/noise grids, metrics, feature budgets, preprocessing, and baseline training settings: 30 epochs with Adam at learning rate 0.001. CIFAR-100 reuses the existing CIFAR preprocessing and feature-budget design without introducing a distinct evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The parameter-estimation, iteration, sample-size, and noise-level analyses in Section 5.1 and Figures 1–2 remain unchanged in design. The Table 1 value correction changes a result, while CIFAR-100 adds benchmark validation without a new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 independent runs for simulation estimation errors and feature-recovery accuracy. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing changes appear; the added benchmark follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add a full CIFAR-100 accuracy and timing comparison, with PPCA leading after feature selection. At 2,000 features, PPCA reports 73.01%, FSA 70.09%, and TISP 70.82%. Table 1 also changes ELF recovery accuracy from 10% to 100% at n=1,000 with 10 noise features. Existing CIFAR-10 and ImageNet results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The model definitions, assumptions A1–A3, Theorems 1–4, and Propositions 1–3 retain their mathematical content. Equation splitting and renumbering are presentational. The added prior-work SNR formula and informal scalability discussion introduce no new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain stable. The introduction strengthens the scalability claim by explicitly contrasting O(C) margin-based learning with O(1) addition of an independent class model. The conclusion also extends its empirical claim from CIFAR-10 to the CIFAR datasets.

C2.justification: The introduction adds the explanation that individual models tightly surround their class observations, connecting this geometry to independent class addition. Section 5.2 extends the SVD-cost explanation and PPCA efficiency interpretation to CIFAR-100. Existing limitations and recovery-bound ambitions remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The added CIFAR-100 experiment is documented as using 144×144 images and average-pooled, 2,560-dimensional CLIP RN50x4 features; Tables 3–4 supply its runtimes. Existing hardware, optimizer, and source-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of the already cited Huang–Liao and Mishra–Sahu SNR approaches, explaining their criterion and contrasting their stated lack of recovery guarantees with this paper's per-class formulation. A CIFAR-100 reference is added; other works are retained through renumbering.

P1.justification: Targeted edits expand the introduction, SNR related-work discussion, and experimental narrative, while shortening and refining the conclusion. Cross-references are updated, but the six-section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2–4 gain CIFAR-100 blocks. Figure 3 expands from two to three smaller panels and moves to the upper right of page 8. Equations, algorithms, and surrounding text are locally rearranged; Figures 1–2 retain identical plots.

improvement.justification: CIFAR-100 adds useful validation with a different leading method, the Table 1 correction resolves an anomalous ELF entry, and the expanded related work clarifies novelty. These are limited improvements to evidence and exposition. The new CIFAR-100 prose compares PPCA's peak with the baselines' full-feature scores despite better baseline scores elsewhere in Table 2, weakening the fairness of that presentation.
